summary: DEF-006. Re-issues public.get_bank_connection_health_for_org(uuid) from its live body, aliasing and qualifying the two references in its authorisation check that collided with the OUT parameter of the same name. Every call previously aborted with 42702. Signature, volatility, security mode, search_path and the returned column list are unchanged.

problem.symptom: /bookkeeping fires this RPC three times per load and every call fails with `42702 column reference "organization_id" is ambiguous`. Bank connection health is never displayed.
problem.root_cause: The function's RETURNS TABLE list declares an OUT parameter named organization_id. Inside the authorisation check the same name is written unqualified (`WHERE user_id = auth.uid() AND organization_id = _org_id`), so PostgreSQL cannot tell whether it means the OUT parameter or organization_users' column.
problem.gate_6: The user never learns. The page ignores the failure and renders as though every connection were healthy, so an expired consent or a broken feed is indistinguishable from a working one. The app-side half of this release fixes that separately: the overview card previously fell back to an empty list and announced 'No bank connections across the practice yet' — a hard failure rendered as reassurance.
problem.fix_choice: Aliased and qualified rather than `#variable_conflict use_column`. The pragma silently changes how EVERY unqualified name in the body resolves; the alias changes exactly the two references that are wrong and leaves the rest provably alone.

live_bodies_used.basis: Fetched via MCP catalog_functions(include_source: true) and reproduced verbatim except the two qualifications in the authorisation EXISTS.

expected_objects.object: get_bank_connection_health_for_org(uuid) returns rows instead of raising 42702
expected_objects.verify_via: catalog_functions(name_like: 'get_bank_connection_health_for_org', include_source: true) -> def-hash CHANGED from 7012eeed15ee414c3bec6df9d574ad9d; body contains `organization_users ou` and `ou.organization_id = _org_id`. Then db_rpc it with a real organization id and confirm a result set (possibly empty) rather than an error.

expected_objects.object: A caller who is not a member of the organization still gets 42501 'forbidden'
expected_objects.verify_via: Call it with an organization id the signed-in user does NOT belong to and confirm it still raises forbidden. The change touches the authorisation check itself, so this is the regression that would matter — a qualification mistake could turn the EXISTS into something always true.

expected_objects.object: /bookkeeping displays connection health, and displays an explicit error state when it cannot
expected_objects.verify_via: Load /bookkeeping and confirm the Practice Banking Health card lists connections. Then confirm the failure path is distinguishable from the empty path — with the RPC failing, the card must say health is unavailable, not 'No bank connections across the practice yet'.

rollback.assessment: Forward-only. Restoring 7012eeed reinstates a function that cannot execute at all, so there is no scenario in which rolling back is preferable.
rollback.data_risk: None. The function is STABLE and reads only; the migration changes name resolution, not behaviour.

steps: Apply 20260728160000_fix_bank_connection_health_ambiguity.sql via the Lovable migration flow.
Confirm the card returns green AND a row exists in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations (verify against LIVE, not just Test).
Verify the forbidden path FIRST — an authorisation check was edited.
Then load /bookkeeping and confirm health is displayed.
After apply: refresh docs/audits/unapplied-migrations-baseline.json with the new applied version.
Notify Claude to run the expected-object verification and complete this receipt (move out of pending/).

post_apply_followups: get_bank_connection_health_for_entity was NOT examined. It is the sibling RPC used on the entity-level view and may carry the same OUT-parameter collision; it should be checked against its live body before the bookkeeping module is described as working.

The audit's remaining DEF-006 actions — verifying the connected, disconnected, expired, degraded and no-connection states individually — need real connection fixtures and are not covered by this release.
